content: Second, the linked entities may also be too common to be considered an entity. This may introduce errors and irrelevance to the summary. In the example, “Wednesday” is erroneous because it is wrongly linked to the entity “Wednesday Night Baseball”. Also, “swap” is irrelevant because although it is linked correctly to the entity “Trade (Sports)”, it is too common and irrelevant when generating the summaries. In our experimental data, we randomly select 100 data instances and tag the correctness and relevance of extracted entities into one of four labels: A: correct and relevant, B: correct and somewhat relevant, C: correct but irrelevant, and D: incorrect. Results show that $29.4\%$ , $13.7\%$ , $30.0\%$ , and $26.9\%$ are tagged with A, B, C, and D, respectively, which shows that there is a large amount of incorrect and irrelevant entities.
